2026-06-18 cross-session auto-retry for stuck private-receive entries (#9, designed + adversarially verified). PROBLEM: a private index entry that the per-session 3-strikes unknown-error skip buries (cursor advances past it; the in-memory strike Map dies on reload, so a reload starting from the advanced cursor never re-scans it) was permanently lost unless the user hit 'Sync messages'. FIX (all web/app.js, v434): a NEW persistent localStorage store ('platho.private.chain.stuck.entry.v1', keyed by hub+keyId, records {entryId, strikes, lastError, firstSeen/lastSeen}) mirroring the body-history-unavailable store. The 3-strikes ELSE now persists the skipped entry (rememberPrivateStuckEntry, returns the cross-session strike); its ids are UNIONed into the existing retryEntryIds replay set (re-scanned each session regardless of the advanced cursor); the record is cleared on genuine success (empty / open-ok, NOT before the open); after PRIVATE_SCAN_UNKNOWN_ERROR_CROSS_SESSION_CAP=8 cross-session strikes the entry is PROMOTED to a surfaced 'undelivered' gap (filtered out of the replay set so it is re-fetched 0 times thereafter) and surfaced via a new undeliveredCount (read from the STORE, not the per-run skipped counter, so it survives reload) wired into privateSyncResult + privateSyncStatusText ('N undelivered') + the completeMessageSyncUi gate + the reason ladder ('private_entry_undelivered'). THE LOAD-BEARING CORRECTION (both adversarial verdicts): the retryEntryIds replay loop does `if (!result.ok) break`, so a stuck id fed in must NOT return {ok:false} (would stall the whole pass + cursor every session — a worse loop than v419-v421). scanPrivateEntryId now has a fast-path: a persisted/replayed stuck entry (alreadyStuck = source==='history-retry' || hasPrivateStuckEntry) on re-fail bumps the persistent strike and returns {ok:true} immediately (one read, never scanComplete=false), mirroring body-history's non-blocking contract; only a FRESH index-walk unknown error keeps the per-session 3-strikes ramp. BOUNDED (no poison loop): the cursor write gate is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED (recovery is the replay set, not cursor manipulation); per-session replay is capped by AUTO_LIMIT=2 + the 3-min cooldown; lifetime re-fetches per entry <= CAP=8 then 0 (the strikes>=CAP filter sits BEFORE the cooldown so promoted ids never consume the auto budget). Manual 'Sync messages' (forceHistoryRetry/forceIndexRescan) uses the manual limit (16) for the stuck set too. Test PWA-RECEIVE-RETRY-01; PWA-CONFIG-07B retry-set assertions updated for the union + the ternary scan-log. app v433->v434, SW cache v504->v505; deploy-prep regenerated. This completes the send/receive reliability arc (v430 activation -> v431 burst-send/gateway -> v432 receive-gap -> v433 double-publish -> v434 cross-session retry). npm.cmd test = 114/114 test files, 1002/1002 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).

2026-06-18 double-publish / double-spend hardening (after an adversarially-verified multi-agent investigation that NARROWED the risk: the broad public-double and nonce-floor theories were REFUTED as reachable; exactly ONE live path remained). MECHANISM (#1, rare but irreversible): a private publish part broadcast at nonce N gets an AMBIGUOUS result (5xx/timeout) but ACTUALLY lands; ~150s later the receipt ring slot (nonce%20) is evicted so confirmVaultBatchReceiptsFromPublishState misses it; recoverDroppedSignedPublishParts then asks provePublishPartAbsentFromSenderIndex, which in DEGRADED-verification survival mode (common on RU networks: keyless toncenter 403/429 → one unverified replica) read a lagging replica that had not yet indexed the landed entry → returned 'absent' → the part was cleared + reset to BUILT + fresh-re-signed at the now-advanced nonce N+1 → the SAME private entry published twice + double TON spend. FIVE fixes (all web/app.js): (1) provePublishPartAbsentFromSenderIndex is now FAIL-CLOSED — it returns 'inconclusive' (never 'absent') when tonRpcVerificationStructurallyDegraded(), and forces verify:true/allowUnverifiedCriticalRead:false; so a fresh re-sign can only follow a VERIFIED absence proof. (2) before any clear+reset, recoverDroppedSignedPublishParts cross-checks the kind-agnostic receipt ring with a VERIFIED read — CONFIRMED→confirm (no re-sign), any non-EVICTED status (PROCESSING/REJECTED/BOUNCED)→no re-sign, only a missing/EVICTED receipt + verified 'absent' authorizes the re-sign; a failed verified receipt read also blocks it. (3) the ambiguous batch-publish catch now raises vaultPublishNonceFloor (cross-path consistency with the success path + single-external helpers). (4) the LATENT public-part hole is guarded by construction (provePublishPartAbsentFromSenderIndex + recoverDroppedSignedPublishParts both skip non-private parts) — not reachable today (recover's only caller is the private confirm driver) but safe if public dropped-recovery is ever wired. (5) a non-'absent'/inconclusive consumed-nonce part is NEVER re-signed — it stays UNKNOWN, keeps idempotently re-broadcasting its one real external, and the existing 15-min partial-retry-deadline surfaces it as a manual-retry block (no silent loss, no auto-double-spend). TRADEOFF (owner-confirmed): in degraded verification a genuinely-dropped message can no longer auto-fresh-resign — it relies on idempotent same-nonce re-broadcast + manual retry; this trades a longer degraded-mode pending window for the absolute no-double-spend guarantee. Test PWA-DOUBLEPUBLISH-01 pins all four guards. app v432->v433, SW cache v503->v504; deploy-prep regenerated. PENDING follow-up: cross-session auto-retry for stuck receive entries (the precise/prompt blocked-state surfacing is the deferred refinement of #5). npm.cmd test = 114/114 test files, 1001/1001 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).

2026-06-18 private RECEIVE-delivery-gap fix (after an adversarially-verified multi-agent investigation of: sender shows all messages 'published' but a recipient that reports '✓ Synced' is permanently missing a non-contiguous subset, incl. an image). ROOT: receive-side truthfulness + permanent-drop — completeMessageSyncUi (web/app.js) reported 'synced' while per-entry skip paths dropped entries, and the cursor advanced past them (permanent across sessions). PRIMARY trigger: a transient RPC_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE error ('TON RPC verification unavailable') was matched by isPrivateOpenKeyMismatchError's /unavailable/i and routed into the PERMANENT unreadable-capsule branch (reason private_key_open_failed + cursor advance) → dropped forever while the header said 'Synced'; each entry fails independently → the non-contiguous shape; the v430 recipient under a /messages 429 storm (the same storm v431 #5 fixed for the SENDER path) generated exactly these errors. THREE fixes (all web/app.js, v432): (1) honest 'Synced' — completeMessageSyncUi now also gates on Number(skipped)===0 + Number(incompletePrivateStreamCount)===0 + the reasons private_key_open_failed/partial_stream_pending/index_limit_without_cursor, so the header shows 'delayed'/'message parts pending'/'message key mismatch' instead of a false '✓ Synced'; (2) transient-not-permanent — a transient guard (isTonRpcVerificationSoftReadError || isTonRpcTransientError) sits BEFORE the unreadable branch in scanPrivateEntryId and returns {ok:false} (pins the cursor → re-walk next cycle once RPC recovers) instead of dropping; the 'unavailable' token was removed from isPrivateOpenKeyMismatchError; only deterministic crypto/structural mismatches remain permanently-unreadable (correct, decrypt is hash-verified-before-decrypt so it cannot intermittently fail); (3) multipart surfacing — incompletePrivateStreamCount is now plumbed into privateSyncResult + the gate + privateSyncStatusText ('message parts pending') so a stale incomplete multipart (an image) never reports a clean 'Synced'. REFUTED (not the cause): anonymous-thread mis-filing (those messages are visible in a separate thread), dedup collision (content-addressed), transient-decrypt (hash verified before AES-GCM). Tests: new PWA-DELIVERY-01 (the honest-Synced gate) + updated PWA-CONFIG-07D (transient guard before the unreadable branch + the 'unavailable' token gone). app v431->v432, SW cache v502->v503; deploy-prep regenerated (prod bundle c7c220e9..., productionReady=true). 2026-06-15 RPC verifier 429 graceful-degradation fix. After the genesis migration the keyless toncenter verifier (the second of the two dual-provider read transports, ~1 rps) answered 429 under sync load; noteTonRpcTransportFailure only parked verifier-only transports on 401/403, never on 429 (isTonRpcHardTransportError excludes 429), so isVerificationDegraded() stayed false, criticalChainReadOptions kept requesting verification, and every critical read (private index sync, getPrivateEntry confirmation, getAvatar hydration) re-hit the throttled verifier and threw RPC_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE -- which spun the publish confirmation-retry loop (re-broadcasts that occasionally hit transient toncenter 500s, since broadcast has no read-fallback). Fix (web/vault-ton-rpc-provider.mjs): a verifier-only transport that answers 429/RATE_LIMITED now parks for the same long window as a 401/403 denial, so verification degrades to the live gateway and reads stop re-hammering the throttled host. Regression test VAULT-RPC-04I8B mirrors the 403 park test with a 429 verifier (parks immediately, isVerificationDegraded true, single verifier probe, unverified reads still flow). vault-ton-rpc-provider.mjs bumped v38->v39 across its 8 importers, service-worker cache v494->v495. npm.cmd test passed locally with 111/111 test files and 986/986 tests (0 failed, 0 skipped).
